Tenant  
  id, name, slug, created\_at

IngestionBatch  
  id, tenant, source\_type (SAP/UTILITY/TRAVEL), uploaded\_by  
  uploaded\_at, file\_name, row\_count, error\_count, status  
  raw\_file (FileField to S3/local)

EmissionRecord  
  id, tenant, batch (FK → IngestionBatch)  
  scope (1/2/3), category (fuel/electricity/flights/hotels/ground)  
  activity\_value (Decimal), activity\_unit (raw, e.g. "L", "kWh", "km")  
  normalized\_value (Decimal), normalized\_unit ("kgCO2e")  
  emission\_factor, emission\_factor\_source  
  period\_start (Date), period\_end (Date)  
  source\_row\_id (the original row identifier from the file)  
  raw\_data (JSONField — store the entire original row)  
  status (pending/approved/rejected/flagged)  
  flag\_reason (nullable text)  
  approved\_by (FK → User, nullable), approved\_at  
  is\_locked (bool — set True after audit sign-off)  
  created\_at, updated\_at

AuditLog  
  id, record (FK → EmissionRecord), action (created/edited/approved/rejected/locked)  
  performed\_by (FK → User), performed\_at, note, before\_value (JSON), after\_value (JSON)

**Key decisions to document:**

* `raw_data` JSONField preserves the original row forever — source of truth  
* `normalized_unit` is always `kgCO2e` — one unit to rule them all  
* `is_locked` is one-way — once True, the record cannot be edited (enforce in serializer \+ model save)  
* Scope 1 \= direct fuel combustion, Scope 2 \= purchased electricity, Scope 3 \= business travel  
* `period_start/end` handles non-calendar billing periods correctly

**Ingestion pipeline — one class per source:**

For each source, write a `Parser` class with a single method: `parse(file) → List[dict]`. Each dict is one normalized row. Then a `Normalizer` class that takes that dict and produces an `EmissionRecord`.

SAP parser handles: stripping BOM characters, detecting German column headers and remapping them, parsing `YYYYMMDD` dates, converting `L → kgCO2e` using a fuel emission factor table.

Utility parser handles: detecting the date column format (DD/MM/YYYY vs ISO), splitting multi-tariff rows, converting kWh → kgCO2e using the grid emission factor for the country/region.

Travel parser handles: looking up IATA codes to lat/lon (embed a small static JSON of the top 500 airports), calculating haversine distance, applying cabin-class multiplier, parsing hotel nights × an average hotel emission factor.

**Key API endpoints:**  
POST /api/batches/upload/        → accepts file, source\_type; triggers parsing  
GET  /api/batches/               → list all batches for tenant  
GET  /api/batches/{id}/records/  → paginated records for a batch  
GET  /api/records/               → all records, filterable by status/scope/date  
PATCH /api/records/{id}/approve/ → set status=approved, lock  
PATCH /api/records/{id}/reject/  → set status=rejected \+ flag\_reason  
GET  /api/records/summary/       → aggregate kgCO2e by scope/category for dashboard  
GET  /api/audit-log/             → full audit trail

**Flag suspicious rows automatically** in the normalizer:

* Value is 0 or negative  
* Unit couldn't be recognized  
* Date is in the future or more than 3 years old  
* Value is \>3 standard deviations from the batch mean (compute after all rows parsed)

[Decision.md](http://Decision.md)

1. SAP: chose flat-file CSV over IDoc/OData (no middleware required, matches real client export behavior)  
2. SAP: chose to handle fuel (`WERKS` plant codes) and procurement commodity spend, skipped HR/payroll tables  
3. Utility: chose CSV over PDF because PDF parsing is brittle; chose to handle electricity only, not gas/water  
4. Travel: chose CSV export format over live Concur API (API requires OAuth corporate account)  
5. Travel: handle flights \+ hotels \+ ground transport; skip rail (complex factor tables)  
6. Dates: always store UTC, always store `period_start + period_end` as a range  
7. Emission factors: use DEFRA 2023 factors (publicly available, auditor-recognized)

[Tradeoffs.md](http://Tradeoffs.md)

* Live API pull from SAP OData — would need SAP credentials and middleware; file upload covers 95% of real client onboarding  
* Multi-currency normalization — stored amounts in source currency; emission calculation doesn't depend on money so this doesn't affect accuracy  
* Real-time Concur/Navan OAuth integration — their API requires enterprise approval; CSV export is the practical path for a prototype

**Utility:**

* Search "UK utility bill CSV export format fields" for realistic column names

**Travel:**

* DEFRA 2023 air travel factors: DEFRA doc, "Business travel — air" sheet  
* Airport IATA codes \+ coordinates: `ourairports.com/data/airports.csv` (free, downloadable)  
* Haversine formula in Python: `pip install haversine`  
* DEFRA hotel emission factors: DEFRA doc, "Hotels" row

NOTE  
**Data Normalization & Storage**:

* raw\_data JSONField preserves the original row forever — it is the source of truth.  
* normalized\_unit is always kgCO2e — one unit to rule them all.  
* **Emission Factors**: We will use placeholders for now (e.g., 1 L fuel \= 2.68 kgCO2e, 1 kWh \= 0.5 kgCO2e, 1 km \= 0.14 kgCO2e).  
* **Scopes**: Scope 1 \= direct fuel combustion, Scope 2 \= purchased electricity, Scope 3 \= business travel.  
* period\_start/end handles non-calendar billing periods.  
* is\_locked is one-way — once True (after approval), the record cannot be edited (enforced in serializer \+ model save).

Normalization:

**`column_resolver.py`** — The semantic column detector. Has \~300 aliases across all three sources. When it sees `tour_id`, it fuzzy-matches it to `trip_id` (score \> 82). When it sees `MEINS` it maps to `unit`. When it sees `Buchungsdatum` it maps to `posting_date`. Used by every normalizer before a single value is touched.

**`date_parser.py`** — Handles 8 date formats: SAP `YYYYMMDD`, Microsoft `/Date(epoch)/`, German `DD.MM.YYYY`, ISO with/without time, US `MM/DD/YYYY`, named `15-Apr-2025`, and dateutil fallback. Returns `(date, flag_message)` — never silently fails.

**`unit_normalizer.py`** — Four normalizer functions, one per domain. Contains DEFRA 2023 emission factors, ICAO 8% flight uplift, grid factors for IN/GB/US/DE, cabin class multipliers, and the haversine calculation. All logic is in plain Python with no hidden magic — fully defensible in interview.

**`normalize.py`** — The main pipeline. Calls the above three. Key techniques from the PDF:

* `_interpolate_billing_period()` — splits billing periods across calendar months via daily prorating  
* BWART `313`/`315` skip logic — prevents double-counting internal SAP transfers  
* kVA demand charge exclusion — they become `SKIP` records, not Scope 2  
* Negative kWh → `exported_renewable_energy` category (not subtracted from Scope 2\)  
* `_outlier_flags()` — z-score \>3 across batch marks records FLAGGED  
* `_dedup()` — SHA-256 hash of each source row detects SAP batch-rerun duplicates  
* Booking status filtering — `A_NOTF` (not submitted) rows are excluded from carbon totals

**Export Workflow**: The flow will strictly follow: Raw Upload \-\> Normalized \-\> Flagged \-\> Analyst Reviewed \-\> Approved \-\> Exportable.

* **Formats**: Both CSV and XLSX.  
* **Delivery**: Direct download or Email (mocked via filebased email backend).  
* **Tracking**: ExportLog will track who exported, when, type, row count, and filters.

* Approve rows, confirm they become locked.
